about: The cause of each kind of difference and of each not-comparable kind in the run of 2026-11-01, as far as the data shows it, written by the reader after reading the results (acceptance/runs/2026-11-01/results.json) and the files they name. Keyed by comparison|field|result; '*' stands for every field of that comparison and result.
b-json|Age|differ: The registry's own CSV, not TrialLedger. The documentation of the CSV (acceptance/csv-columns.md) lists MinimumAge, MaximumAge and StdAge for the Age column; the CSV the API sent holds only the age groups (StdAge), joined by ", ". The column differs for exactly the 16 studies whose record states a minimum or a maximum age, and agrees for the 4 that state neither. TrialLedger's workbooks are not involved: record.xlsx states minimumAge and maximumAge as the JSON holds them (comparison a, all agree) and review.xlsx's Minimum Age and Maximum Age columns agree with them (comparison c). The CSV columns TrialLedger's studies.csv holds are the API's own, so the same omission is in studies.csv (comparison d).
c-rows|Outcome Results|omitted: NCT06145282's results section registers five outcome measures; three (secondary: "Event-free Survival and Overall Survival", "Viral Reactivation and Disease", "Autoimmune and Hyperinflammatory Complications") have reportingStatus NOT_POSTED and no classes, categories or measurements. review.xlsx's Outcome Results sheet, which its About sheet describes as "every posted outcome measurement, per group", has no row for them. Every value of the three (type, title, reporting status, time frame, units selected) is in record.xlsx (comparison a agrees for each), and the same three outcomes are in review.xlsx's Outcomes sheet from the protocol section, but nothing in review.xlsx says that the results section holds them as not yet posted. Within the sheet's stated scope this is not a posted value left out; by this test's accounting, in which every outcome measure of the results section stands for at least one row, it is an element no row stands for, and it is reported as it falls. The reader cannot tell from the outputs whether the omission is intended.
d|studies.csv|differ: studies.csv is not the API's CSV byte for byte: it is the API's bytes for the same query with a UTF-8 byte-order mark (EF BB BF) put before them. After those three bytes, every one of its 102 lines is identical byte for byte to the API's (the line results of comparison d all agree). The registry sent no byte-order mark to any request this reader made: the run's own fetch, and the eight requests of acceptance/runs/2026-11-01/bom-probe.json (page sizes 100, 1000 and the default, with and without countTotal; Accept: text/csv; Accept-Encoding: identity; another User-Agent); every full answer there is exactly studies.csv without its first three bytes. So the mark is added on TrialLedger's side, not sent by the registry. AGENTS.md says pull saves "the registry's own spreadsheet of them byte for byte (studies.csv)"; by three bytes it does not. Whether the mark is intended (spreadsheet programs read a UTF-8 file with one correctly) the reader cannot tell from the outputs; trialledger verify certifies the folder with it.
d|studies.csv byte-order mark|differ: The same three bytes as above, named on their own: a UTF-8 byte-order mark begins studies.csv and not the API's CSV.
a-title|*|not_comparable: The registry's metadata (/studies/metadata, vendored as TrialLedger/registry/ctg-metadata.json) gives no title for these fields (for example geoPoint.lat and lon, otherEvents[].term, a measure's groups[].id and denoms[]); in every one of these rows record.xlsx's Field column holds the field's own name ("lat", "term", "groupId"), so there is no title of the registry's to compare it with. The Value of each of these rows is compared in comparison a, and agrees.
reader_changes: Before the selection, the reader looked at the shape of TrialLedger's outputs on a three-trial pull of NCT04852770, NCT01030536 and NCT00033111, none of which is among the twenty, and tried the selection's query forms against the registry; nothing of the twenty was pulled or compared before acceptance/selection.json was written.

The first comparison of the twenty showed 66 review.xlsx cells as differing (26 Arms › Interventions Named, 27 Interventions › Arms Named, 13 Interventions › Other Names: "the record holds no value here"). The cause was the reader's: its pattern expansion (expand in compare.py) did not read a fixed index such as armGroups[0], so every list field under a row's own element looked absent. Fixed; the 66 cells then agree. No TrialLedger output changed.

The same first comparison showed 33 review.xlsx rows as differing (14 Adverse Events, 14 Outcome Results, 5 Outcomes: "the row's Location is not an element of this kind"). Each is the one row a sheet writes for a study that has no element of its kind (no results posted, or no outcome registered), stating so. The reader had no rule for such a row; it now has one (placeholder_result): such a row agrees when the study has no element of that kind and the row holds no value in any column declared from a field, and differs otherwise. The 33 rows then agree, counted as absent. No TrialLedger output changed.

The first defects run caught 12 of 13 (acceptance/runs/2026-11-01/defects-first-version.json): comparison (d) compared studies.csv only as a whole file, which already differed by its byte-order mark, so the planted change could not show as a new result. (d) now names the byte-order mark on its own and compares the rest line by line; its whole-file result on the clean folder is unchanged (differ), and the defect is caught at its line. In the same revision each planted defect names every comparison that reads its file (record.xlsx is read by (a) and by (b) against the CSV), so the four results (b) gave for defects 1, 2 and 4 are attributed to them instead of being listed as unattributed.
trialledger verify's output is now kept whole in verify-pull.txt and verify-defects-copy.txt instead of being cut to its last 2,000 characters inside the result; the result itself is unchanged.

After the review of the first commit (2026-11-01), the reader was revised. Each change, and what it moved: (1) Participants at Risk, which review.xlsx declares computed, was taken out of comparison (c) ("columns declared from one registry field"), where its 1,465 cells had been counted as agreeing with numAtRisk, and is now checked with At Risk Source against the rule review.xlsx declares (c-rule): the same 1,465 cells, all following the rule; (c) now counts 22,819 cells instead of 24,284. (2) Six stated columns that were listed as not compared are now compared (c-form): Outcomes › Outcome Type and Order, Adverse Events › Table, Participant Flow › Kind, Publications › Retractions and Studies › Collaborators; their text forms were read from review.xlsx's About sheet. This found the 12 Retractions cells above. (3) Every column the reader compares is now checked against the status and source review.xlsx's About sheet declares for it (c-declared), because the pairings in REVIEW_SHEETS were transcribed from that sheet: 154 columns, all declared stated from the paired field. (4) record.xlsx's Role is checked facet by facet against the record (a-role): 11,610 roles, all holding. (5) The provenance both About sheets state is compared with the registry's /version, the selection and the records (g). (6) Comparison (d) names the header line of studies.csv by "*" instead of by its first eleven bytes ("NCT Number,"); no result changed. (7) Three seeded defects were added for the new checks (a changed Role, a changed provenance date, a changed computed at-risk count). (8) The tests now run on small excerpts of the records written into the test file, not on this run's files. The results.json these replace is kept in summary as runs/2026-11-01/results-superseded-95e84edc8751.json (its SHA-256, the reader's digest, its per-field counts and every result that is not agreement or not comparable), and the defects.json as runs/2026-11-01/defects-superseded-d8685b9e5420.json. The results.json of the very first comparison, before the changes listed above it, was overwritten and not kept, so the 66 and 33 figures above cannot be checked against a kept file.

Later in the same revision, while the reader's decisions were converged with Detective: workbook_text reads an empty record.xlsx cell as empty text, as the CSV writes an absent value, instead of as "None"; csv_expected builds its columns from module tables (CSV_SINGLE, CSV_LISTS, CSV_ITEM_PARTS, DESIGN_PARTS) instead of tables inside the function, with the same columns and pieces; and acceptance/__init__.py was added so that acceptance/select.py is imported as acceptance.select, never as the standard library's select (select.py's own bytes, and so its SHA-256 in selection.json, are unchanged). No result moved: the comparison before these changes and after them both gave 88,225 results, 5,667 not agreement, and 380 agreeing cells in (b) against record.xlsx.
c-form|Publications › Retractions|differ: No reference of these four studies lists a retraction (the record has no retractions field under any of their 12 references), and every Retractions cell says "none in the record". The value agrees in substance: the record holds none and the cell says so. It is counted as a difference because the absence words review.xlsx's About sheet defines under "how to read" are "not reported", "not applicable to this study type" and "redacted (withheld study)" (and a blank), and "none in the record" is not among them; this column alone uses it. Whether it should read "not reported", or the About sheet should list it, is for the founder; the reader does not treat an undeclared wording as absence.
record_role: Role. record.xlsx's About sheet declares Role "stated", with the source "the role the record's structure gives the value (ledger.node_role)": a TrialLedger rule, not a field of the record, and its values are composites that sit at no single location ("arm=Arm A", "group=OG000; outcome_type=SECONDARY", "event_table=serious; group=EG000"). The same About sheet defines "stated" as "read from a structured field of the record; the column's source names it" and "computed" as "derived by the named rule from the named fields", so by its own definitions Role reads as computed. The reader reports this as found, a question for the founder, and does not reclassify it. What the reader can check it does (a-role): every facet a Role states names a value of an element enclosing the row's location (an arm's label, an intervention's name, a reference's type, an outcome's section or type, an adverse-event table, a group id). It cannot check that a row without a facet should have had one. Category, declared computed from the API metadata's section and module names, is not compared.
g|*|not_comparable: These are TrialLedger's statements about its own run: when it retrieved the records, the tool and writer versions, its code commit and code root, and the digests that bind the folder. The registry states none of them, so there is nothing of the registry's to compare them with; the digests are re-derived by trialledger verify (comparison e), which certifies the folder.
